ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure is a seven-segment digital clock/watch display, which reads 10:20 when viewed upright. Reasoning: When Elisa left the cave at night, the digital clock displayed 10:20 upright, so the departure time was 10:20 at night. After she returned in the morning, she looked at the watch while hanging upside down, and what she saw from the upside-down perspective was still 10:20; therefore the actual display of the watch should be the time obtained by rotating the 10:20 she saw by 180 degrees. After the seven-segment digits are rotated and the left-right order is reversed, the seen 1 0 : 2 0 corresponds to the actual display 0 2 : 0 1, that is, 02:01 in the early morning. From 10:20 at night to midnight is 1 hour 40 minutes, and from midnight to 2:01 in the early morning is 2 hours 1 minute, for a total of 3 hours 41 minutes.

raw_record.question_text: When the bat Elisa left its cave at night, the digital clock showed <image1>. When she came back in the morning and hung herself upside down, she looked at her watch and saw <image1>. How long did she stay out of the cave?

method.method_draft: Read the visible digital-clock image as the upright seven-segment time 10:20. From the text, take this as the departure time at night, i.e. 10:20 PM. For the return, use the fact that Elisa is hanging upside down: if she sees the watch as 10:20, the actual watch display must be the 180-degree rotation of that seen display. Rotate/reverse the seven-segment digits: the seen digits 1 0 : 2 0 correspond to an actual display 0 2 : 0 1, so the return time is 02:01 AM. Compute elapsed time from 10:20 PM to 2:01 AM: 1h40m to midnight plus 2h01m after midnight, totaling 3h41m.
